quotes.text: Learn how to save Amazon Pay details and charge your customers later.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: This guide describes how to save Amazon Pay payment details using
Create a Checkout Session in `setup` mode
Your custom payment form must present a written notice of authorization before confirming
We recommend that you use the following text for your custom payment form:
Check that the `PaymentIntent` has a status of `requires_action` and the type for `next_action` is `redirect_to_url`.
When confirming a PaymentIntent, use the same payment method ID from the previous SetupIntent or PaymentIntent object.

findings: New raw lines 5-17 retain only the subject and four variant routes (Checkout, Direct API, mobile iOS, mobile Android). The old raw lines 8-1143 carry the actual variants; the new index does not establish new API behavior, remove those older behaviors, or validate the linked November variant bodies.

Existing source lines 13, 17-33 reasonably summarize the dated old flow but frontmatter lines 4-7 and Raw Sources line 37 omit the 2026-11-07 index provenance; add the new raw as navigation-only while keeping the 2026-05-07 full capture distinct.

Existing source line 27 says the merchant must display a specific quoted authorization text. Old raw lines 29-40 require permission, terms, opt-in, and a written record; lines 208-216 require a written notice before confirmation but expressly recommend the sample wording. iOS lines 741-747 and Android lines 1011-1021 likewise label their sample words recommended. Correct the necessity of notice without converting example text into mandatory exact wording.

Existing source line 25 calls redirect_to_url Amazon Pay's next_action generally. Old raw lines 386-444 place requires_action/next_action.redirect_to_url on an optional manually redirected PaymentIntent; the SetupIntent browser method in old raw lines 362-384 has a client redirect and return_url, not the same shown next_action JSON. Scope the statement to the documented PaymentIntent branch and keep return or requires_action separate from verified payment success.

Existing source line 13 compresses path-specific behavior. Old raw lines 88-120 use hosted Checkout Session mode setup and customer authorization; lines 225-260 and 362-384 use a Direct API SetupIntent with customer identity, usage, and stripe.confirmAmazonPaySetup; lines 453-527 use a PaymentIntent with setup_future_usage and conditional mandate_data; iOS lines 759-785 and Android lines 1023-1075 use different client SDK confirmation methods.

Old raw lines 46-85, 225-260, 532-574, 695-739, 919-1008 show customer-configured Accounts v2 and Customers v1 alternatives; Accounts v2 availability is dated, customer_account belongs to that branch, customer to v1. Existing source lines 19-23 omit the identity fork, and its Checkout example represents Customers v1 specifically. Preserve this qualifier in any source correction.

Old raw lines 118-120 describe SetupIntent requires_action to succeeded for a test; lines 444 and 532-574 separately require payment-status verification and a later confirmed PaymentIntent for charging. Neither setup completion nor browser return itself proves a successful later charge.

Existing concept wiki/concepts/stripe-amazon-pay.md lines 8-60 addresses the separate 2026-05-13 subscription guide and explicitly dates its contradictions. Its source list line 60 does not yet route to this future-payment source; a concept cross-route may be useful, without merging the two guides or treating November's link index as new behavioral authority.

source_assessments.reason: The raw delta is navigation-only, but the current summary has material baseline overstatements and lacks the newly captured index provenance. A targeted source correction is needed without treating omitted November variant bodies as deprecation or new instructions.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/amazon-pay/set-up-future-payments, new raw lines 5-17 establish the save-for-later subject and routes to Checkout, Direct API, iOS, and Android, but no variant-body prerequisites or confirmation states. The dated old raw lines 29-40, 88-120, 225-260, 362-384, 453-574, 759-785, and 1023-1129 document consent and written terms, hosted Checkout setup, Direct API SetupIntent or PaymentIntent saving, platform-specific client confirmation, and a later PaymentIntent using the saved PaymentMethod. Accounts v2 customer_account and Customers v1 customer are separate identity choices; SetupIntent completion and browser return do not prove the later charge. source-stripe-amazon-pay-set-up-future-payments.md summarizes these paths at lines 13-33 but overstates the exact sample authorization text and broadens the manual PaymentIntent redirect detail.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/amazon-pay/set-up-future-payments, new raw lines 9-17 are presentation and variant navigation, with no proven substantive API change against old raw lines 8-1143. source-stripe-amazon-pay-set-up-future-payments.md should retain the May 2026 Checkout, Direct API, iOS, Android, customer identity, consent, and detach claims as dated history while recording the November index separately. Its lines 25 and 27 need reciprocal qualifications: old raw lines 386-444 show redirect_to_url for an optional PaymentIntent in requires_action, while old raw lines 208-216 require written notice but recommend the quoted wording. The old raw line 212 first-save timing conflicts with lines 210 and 1013-1015. Neither old SDK examples nor the uncaptured November variant links establish current runtime behavior, authorization outcome, payment success, or account eligibility.
